faq.a: Samat is associated with the Arabic form صَمَد, whose core sense is samat; eternal, everlasting.

faq.q: What is the origin of Samat?
faq.a: Samat is associated with Arabic. Samat is Arabic صَمَد (Ṣamad), meaning 'eternal, everlasting'. It is widely used as a male given name in Central Asia.
Yes — the underlying form صَمَد is Arabic.
Samat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Samat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ص م د is Quranic, but Ṣamad is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Samat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Samat is rendered صمد and carries the sense صمد، بی‌نیاز.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Samat, samat. Script forms are صمد, صَمَد, समत.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
